newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta mayor signs 16 pct sewer rate increase.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta mayor signs 16 pct sewer rate increase.

text.p: Atlanta Mayor Bill Campbell has signed an ordinance raising sewer rates by 16 percent to pay debt service on a $180 million bond issue, a spokesman for the mayor said Tuesday.
The increase, which will raise monthly bills by $3.10 a month for the average homeowner, takes effect April 1.

Campbell had originally proposed issuing $505 million of revenue bonds and raising sewer rates by 81 percent to fund upgrades needed to bring the city's water-sewer system in compliance with state environmental laws.
He has since proposed privatizing management of the city's water-sewer system, which he said would generate enough savings to cover the cost of most of the upgrades.
Campbell's plan still calls for the city to issue $180 million of revenue bonds to finance system upgrades that must be completed this year.
The city is under a 90-day moratorium for construction requiring new sewer hookups and faces fines of $20,000 a day for violating state water pollution laws.
The city council approved the smaller rate hike on March 4.
